advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip `--platform=`/other build flags in the FROM branch of DOCKERFILE_IMAGE_PATTERN so platform-qualified FROM lines match the real image, not the flag.
evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py:66: `r"^\s*(?:FROM\s+(?P<from>\S+)|COPY\s+(?:--\S+\s+)*--from=(?P<copy>\S+))"`
The COPY branch consumes flags via `(?:--\S+\s+)*` but the FROM branch `FROM\s+(?P<from>\S+)` has no equivalent, so a `--platform=...` flag is captured as the image reference.
advisory.finding: The FROM alternative in DOCKERFILE_IMAGE_PATTERN captures the first whitespace-delimited token after FROM without skipping optional `--platform=` flags, unlike the COPY alternative which consumes `(?:--\S+\s+)*`. A `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM python:3.12` line captures `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` as the reference, so the actual base image (`python:3.12`) is never scanned; a literal `FROM --platform=linux/amd64 python:latest` captures `--platform=linux/amd64` (contains `/`) and yields a spurious 'names no tag' finding on the flag instead of checking the real image.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add flag-skipping to the FROM branch, mirroring COPY: `FROM\s+(?:--\S+\s+)*(?P<from>\S+)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether ARG/variable-templated image tags should be rejected (they can float via build-arg defaults) rather than silently skipped, or document why they are exempt.
evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py:392: `if "${" in reference or reference.startswith("$"):` then `return False`

A reference like `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}` returns False from _is_registry_reference and is `continue`d over in check_dockerfiles, producing no finding regardless of what UV_VERSION resolves to.
advisory.finding: An image reference whose tag is templated by a build ARG (e.g. `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}` or `FROM python:$PY_TAG`) is treated as a non-registry reference and silently skipped, so an ARG-driven floating uv tag escapes the gate entirely — the check cannot distinguish 'no ARG-pinned uv image present' from 'an ARG-pinned uv image that was skipped'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert on the specific per-finding line (e.g. the file:line detail or the reference text) rather than the substring 'latest' that the trailer always prints.
evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:340: `assert "latest" in result.stderr`

scripts/check_uv_pin.py trailer: `"fetches. Every Dockerfile must pull {UV_IMAGE_REPOSITORY} at that same exact version, and no Dockerfile may resolve any image from a floating :latest tag."` — the word 'latest' is always in stderr when the gate fails.
advisory.finding: test_dockerfile_floating_uv_tag_is_rejected and (implicitly) test_dockerfile_untagged_uv_reference_is_rejected assert `"latest" in result.stderr`, but the always-emitted trailer summary contains the literal 'floating :latest tag', so this substring is present on ANY returncode==1 run. The assertion does not verify the floating-tag finding was actually produced, weakening the test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin docker-compose.langfuse.yml MinIO to an exact version (or extend the gate to cover compose `image:` keys) so the floating-tag drift class is closed everywhere, not only in Dockerfiles.
evidence: docker-compose.langfuse.yml:113: `image: docker.io/minio/minio:latest`
scripts/check_uv_pin.py:433 `def check_dockerfiles(root)` iterates only `_dockerfiles(root)` (glob `**/Dockerfile*`), never compose `image:` keys
Ticket febd-6b13-1976-43be comment: 'docker-compose.langfuse.yml:113 runs image: docker.io/minio/minio:latest. Same defect class ... AC3 as written does not cover it'
advisory.finding: docker-compose.langfuse.yml pins MinIO to a floating `:latest` tag (`image: docker.io/minio/minio:latest`) — the identical floating-image drift defect this change exists to eliminate — but the new gate only scans Dockerfiles, so this compose `image:` key is not covered by any drift guard.
scenarios: A `docker compose -f docker-compose.langfuse.yml up` after upstream publishes a new minio/minio:latest silently changes the running MinIO version, reproducing the same class of untracked drift the ticket was filed for.
make lint stays green while this floating tag persists, so no gate catches the regression.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the real-repository test's directory-skip set with _dockerfiles() in check_uv_pin.py so the test and the enforced gate scan the identical Dockerfile set.
evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:314-317: `for path in sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("**/Dockerfile*")) if ".git/" not in path.as_posix()`
scripts/check_uv_pin.py:398 `skipped = {".git", ".venv", "node_modules", "__pycache__"}`
advisory.finding: The new real-repository test filters only `.git/` when globbing `**/Dockerfile*`, whereas the enforced gate (_dockerfiles) additionally skips `.venv`, `node_modules`, and `__pycache__`; a vendored Dockerfile with a `:latest` tag under one of those dirs would fail the test but be silently ignored by the gate, so the two disagree on scope.
scenarios: A developer with a vendored/checked-in Dockerfile under .venv or node_modules gets a red pytest run that `make lint` (the actual enforcement path) would pass, or vice versa — divergent signals about the same tree.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fixture test that a Dockerfile using a build-arg-interpolated image reference (FROM ${BASE} / COPY --from=${UV_REF}) produces no finding, guarding the _is_registry_reference variable branch.
evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py:392-394: `if "${" in reference or reference.startswith("$"): return False`
No test in tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py writes a Dockerfile with `ARG UV_REF` / `COPY --from=${UV_REF}` or `FROM $BASE` — the added early-return is exercised by no case
advisory.finding: The newly added build-arg/variable branch of _is_registry_reference (references beginning with `$` or containing `${...}`) is untested — no test drives a Dockerfile whose FROM/COPY --from uses an ARG-interpolated reference to confirm it is skipped rather than misclassified as a floating/untagged image.
scenarios: A Dockerfile uses `ARG BASE` + `FROM ${BASE}`; a regression removing this guard would flag it as untagged/floating, breaking make lint on a legitimate build-arg reference

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider pinning the uv image by digest (`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7@sha256:...`) for immutable provenance.
evidence: COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7 /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
scripts/check_uv_pin.py `_image_tag`: "A digest (``image@sha256:...``) is an exact pin, so it reports its own digest as the 'tag' and is accepted."
Same pattern in Dockerfile.opcert and Dockerfile.reviewbot
advisory.finding: The uv distribution image is pinned by mutable tag (`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7`) rather than by immutable digest, so a re-pushed or hijacked 0.12.7 tag would silently change the copied binary; the checker already supports digest pins (`_image_tag` handles `@sha256:`) but the images do not use them.
scenarios: Upstream (or a compromised publisher) re-publishes the 0.12.7 tag with a different binary
Supply-chain integrity audit expecting content-addressable pins

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether base images should also be digest/patch pinned, or document that only the uv toolchain pin is enforced by this gate.
evidence: `_check_dockerfile_reference` only flags `tag is None` and `tag == "latest"` for non-uv images
Fixture base image `FROM python:3.12-slim` passes the clean gate (tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py DOCKERFILE_CLEAN)
Gate summary claims 'no Dockerfile may resolve any image from a floating :latest tag' but `python:3.12-slim` is also floating (tracks latest 3.12 patch)
advisory.finding: The new gate rejects only `:latest`/untagged references, so a floating minor base tag like `python:3.12-slim` passes despite moving across patch releases — the same class of 'time bomb by upstream publish' the change claims to eliminate remains for base images.
scenarios: Upstream publishes a new python:3.12-slim patch that breaks the build or introduces a regression, with no change to this repo

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a digest-pinned uv reference (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv@sha256:...) passes the gate, proving the documented 'digest pins stay allowed' contract and guarding the uv-repo mismatch branch against digest false positives.
evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py:378-379: `if "@" in reference: return reference.split("@", 1)[1]` — a uv digest yields tag 'sha256:...'

scripts/check_uv_pin.py:422-428: `repository = reference.split("@", 1)[0].rsplit(":", 1)[0]` then `if repository == UV_IMAGE_REPOSITORY and version is not None and tag != version:` returns a Finding — a uv digest tag ('sha256:...') != '0.12.7' triggers this
commit message: 'Named build stages (COPY --from=builder) and digest pins stay allowed.'
_image_tag docstring: 'A digest (image@sha256:...) is an exact pin, so it reports its own digest as the "tag" and is accepted.'
search_files for 'sha256' in tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py returned (no matches) — no digest test exists
blocking.finding: The digest-pin acceptance path is untested, and appears broken: the diff documents 'digest pins stay allowed' and _image_tag has a dedicated `@` branch, but for a uv digest reference (e.g. `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv@sha256:...`) _check_dockerfile_reference resolves repository==UV_IMAGE_REPOSITORY with tag='sha256:...' != version, so it returns a Finding and REJECTS the digest. No test exercises a digest reference to prove the documented allowed path.
scenarios: A future Dockerfile pins uv by digest (the documented-allowed exact pin); the gate rejects it and fails make lint despite the pin being valid
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a fixture test writing `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv@sha256:<64hex> /uv /usr/local/bin/uv` and assert returncode == 0; if it fails, correct _check_dockerfile_reference to accept digest references for the uv repository.
